correctness.rationale: In a closed age-state path every juvenile state is bounded by a fertility and a maturation transition; all other transitions contribute p. Choosing these nonoverlapping adjacent pairs gives the cyclic matching expansion. The fixed determinant and positive off-diagonal entries give a strictly trace-increasing Perron root, also for odd periods (negative fixed determinant). For period one the trace is p. At lengths two and three only the fertility sum can enter; at four and five all pairwise differences are a single difference of disjoint-pair sums multiplied by the positive factor s²p^(n−4), with no arithmetic-progression assumption at these shorter lengths. At six the two independent-set sizes give order statistics B,H,C. Fixing 1 at the first position and choosing the smaller of its two neighbors as second partitions all 720 words; independent enumeration agreed with all 60 certificate rows. A uniquely minimizes B, C uniquely maximizes B and attains the other two maxima, and all non-A orbits satisfy B≥94,H≥65,C≥54 with the B-orbit alone attaining both B=94 and C=54. This proves strict dominance over all remaining minima even at a=0. The A-minus-B trace is s²p²d²(2sd/p²−1), so equality gives exactly two orbits. All three published sample comparisons were separately reproduced.
residual_risks: The six-season optimizer classification is for equally spaced, distinct fertilities and common positive maturation and persistence, not arbitrary six-level inventories or transient population measures.

value.rationale: Fixed-inventory extremal growth is a natural scheduling question. The earliest reversal mechanism comes from competition between the two- and three-matching terms. Identifying which inequivalent schedules actually minimize or maximize and determining when the worst changes independently of the fertility baseline gives a benchmark beyond finding one reversible pair. The exhaustive finite work resolves a motivated global problem rather than sampling and extrapolating.
residual_risks: This is a deterministic demographic benchmark, not an empirically validated management recommendation.
